principles: Extend the existing host-neutral observability source of truth instead of replacing it.
Make visual discipline and click resolution explicit acceptance requirements, not optional polish.
Keep the MVP read-only and host-neutral, with Authority boundaries always visible.
Prefer live CLI JSON contracts and recovery commands over static dashboard claims.
drivers: The user asked for a detailed requirements recommendation document, not implementation.
The static demo is useful but currently hard-coded and incomplete as a product contract.
Lattice philosophy requires local evidence, host verdicts, Authority receipts, and production DONE to remain separate.

options.name: A: Add a focused MVP requirements addendum
pros: Preserves the adopted host-neutral observability console document as the source anchor
Captures prototype-specific requirements without rewriting the whole design
Keeps scope small enough for a document-only story
cons: A later implementation story is still required
Some requirements depend on CLI JSON surfaces that may need separate work

options.name: B: Rewrite the existing observability console document
pros: One document would contain all console requirements
cons: Higher risk of disturbing adopted source-of-truth language
More likely to mix prototype productization with authority design

options.name: C: Implement the console immediately
pros: Would produce a visible artifact faster
cons: Violates the current request for a requirements recommendation document
Would prematurely choose adapter and UI architecture
Risks optimizing UI before fixing data and authority correctness

chosen: A: Add a focused MVP requirements addendum
rationale: A focused addendum best satisfies the user request while keeping the existing host-neutral observability design stable and avoiding premature implementation.

preMortem.scenario: The document repeats the existing source of truth instead of adding prototype-specific requirements.
preMortem.trigger: Large sections are copied from host-neutral-observability-console.md without mapping the static demo gaps.
preMortem.consequence: The next implementation story still lacks actionable acceptance criteria.
preMortem.mitigation: Keep this document focused on live data, visual/click requirements, recovery commands, and MVP acceptance.

preMortem.scenario: The document treats visual discipline as optional polish.
preMortem.trigger: Aesthetic spacing, symmetry, and click behavior are not included in acceptance criteria.
preMortem.consequence: A future console could technically read data but still feel untrustworthy or incomplete.
preMortem.mitigation: Make visual rules and click-target inventory mandatory acceptance and verification items.

preMortem.scenario: The document blurs local workflow state with production authority.
preMortem.trigger: Green dashboard states are not explicitly tied to local evidence or verified receipts.
preMortem.consequence: Users may mistake local DONE for productionDone.
preMortem.mitigation: Require global authority markers and per-detail authority explanations.
